problem:
Find the general solution to the equation

$$
{x}^{2}{y}^{″}-11x{y}^{′}+36y=0,\,x>0.
$$
worked_solution:
The given equation is an instance of the Cauchy-Euler equation. So, we assume that the solutions take the form $y={x}^{\lambda }.$ Differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {x}^{\lambda -1},\,{y}^{″}=\lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}.
$$

Substituting the above to our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}\cdot \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda -2}-11x\cdot \lambda {x}^{\lambda -1}+36{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ \lambda (\lambda -1){x}^{\lambda }-11\lambda {x}^{\lambda }+36{x}^{\lambda } & =0 \\ {x}^{\lambda }[\lambda (\lambda -1)-11\lambda +36] & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the auxiliary equation is

$$
\begin{aligned}\lambda (\lambda -1)-11\lambda +36 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2}-12\lambda +36 & =0 \\ (\lambda -6)^{2} & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, we have a double root $\lambda =6.$
Therefore, the general solution is

$$
y(x)={c}_{1}{x}^{6}+{c}_{2}{x}^{6}\operatorname{ln}⁡x.
$$
